issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to a Rideable interface (method messageOnRide()), but the solution repository uses an interface named Mountable instead and the Rideable.java in the solution is empty. Several classes in the solution (Pig, Seal) implement Mountable rather than Rideable, while the template Main and UML/spec expect Rideable. This name/type mismatch (Rideable vs Mountable) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students and can prevent compilation or correct implementation against the provided template/spec.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure consistent interface naming across all artifacts. Rename Mountable in the solution to Rideable (and implement messageOnRide() there), update Pig and Seal to implement Rideable, and populate Rideable.java with the correct method signature. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to use Mountable everywhere, but keep the name consistent so students and provided code reference the same interface type.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to the ride-related interface as 'Rideable' (and students are instructed to implement/use Rideable), but the solution implementation uses an interface named 'Mountable' for the same concept (with messageOnRide()). Additionally, there is an empty Rideable.java file in the solution. This inconsistent naming (Rideable vs Mountable) across artifacts will confuse students when mapping the requirement to the provided solution code and template usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's Mountable interface (and all 'implements Mountable' usages) to Rideable so it matches the problem statement and template. Remove or properly implement the empty Rideable.java in the solution (delete if duplicate, or consolidate and implement the ride interface there). Ensure method signature messageOnRide() remains unchanged.
